- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 2σ above recent 18d mean, reduce by 1–3% to align with historical volatility.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers “reversion” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days, then adjust to sentiment-aligned trend.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 1–2 days; if sentiment turns positive, forecast should rise by 0.5–1.5% in next 24h.
- For 30d horizon, avoid “over-optimistic” peaks: if forecast > 1.5σ above 18d mean, cap at 1.2–1.3x recent 18d average to prevent overshoot.
